extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, photo editors, videographers and other applicants submitting to the NPPA 2026 Best of Photojournalism competition
extracted.subtask_description: Official entry rules and guidelines for the 2026 NPPA Best of Photojournalism contest covering eligibility, ethics/visual integrity, category definitions, judging priorities, technical/file/metadata requirements, and entry procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion of Copyright / Original Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants warrant and represent that each image submitted is their own original work and that they have the unrestricted right to grant the permissions required by the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may be independent photographers or employees; they must be copyright holders or authorized by the copyright holder to submit. This warranty covers every image submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to Use Entries (License to BOP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants grant the Best of Photojournalism (BOP) permission to reproduce, display, publish and distribute submitted entries to promote and carry out BOP mission and may sublicense to third parties as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses include reporting on judging, exhibitions, online displays, awards ceremonies, compendiums (e.g., News Photographer Magazine), educational/research/archiving, and inclusion in permanent archives. BOP is not obligated to publish submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date/Publication Eligibility Window
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must have been taken or initially published during the competition year (Jan 1, 2025–Dec 31, 2025) unless a division/categor y rule states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images/stories may only be entered in one competition year; substantially similar images previously entered cannot be re-entered in a later year. Some categories may ask when material was first published or broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to Rules and Finality of Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: By entering, entrants accept all entry rules and agree that the BOP is the final authority on awards decisions; entrants have no right to appeal judges' or committee decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants explicitly consent and waive claims over use of their name/likeness by BOP and sponsors for related promotional/public relations materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of NPPA Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must adhere to the NPPA Code of Ethics and affirm their entries were created according to its principles; awards may be rescinded if the code was violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must promise compliance on the submission form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Integrity — General Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest places high priority on visual integrity and adherence to ethical standards; visual journalists must maintain the highest ethical standards in daily work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching principle informs capture, editing, presentation, and labeling decisions and is enforced by judging and eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPPA Code of Ethics — Key Standards (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual journalists are accountable to be accurate and comprehensive, resist staged opportunities, provide context, avoid stereotyping and bias, treat subjects with respect and dignity, and be unobtrusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific points: avoid manipulating events, maintain integrity of photographic content/context, do not pay sources, avoid accepting gifts that could influence coverage, do not sabotage colleagues, avoid harassment, defend access rights, and continuously study the craft and ethics. Use this code as the standard for all submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on AI Generative Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of AI generative tools to create, add, remove, expand or alter images or videos in any way is expressly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the photograph or video is considered 'locked' at the moment of recording — what is/was seen or heard cannot be changed with AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Staging, Set-ups, Additions or Removals During Capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographers must not intentionally alter the scene they capture by adding objects, moving/removing objects, staging situations, setting up scenes, or asking subjects to reenact past events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of prohibited behavior include bringing disparate characters together, directing subjects to wear clothing to create a scene, painting/adding objects or people, or asking re-enactments. Portraits and formal interviews are permitted to be constructed only if clearly identified as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portraits & Formal Interviews Must Be Labeled
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits and formal interviews may be constructed, but must be explicitly identified as posed/posed portraits in their captions so they are not presented as candid events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a photograph is a portrait, the caption must clearly state it was posed/directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Processing Limits (allowed vs. prohibited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-processing is permitted within normal limits (toning, color correction, cropping); manipulation that changes content/context is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: basic toning, color correction for white balance/sensor issues, cropping, brightness/contrast/saturation/sharpening within non-content-altering limits. Prohibited: dramatic color changes that alter original scene (e.g., gray sky to blue), dodging/burning or other adjustments that significantly alter content by obscuring/enhancing/diminishing elements, adding/removing/moving objects or people. Cloning tools may only be used to remove dust spots from lens/sensor or scanning artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio/Video Sequencing and Editing Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Altering the sequencing of audio or video in a way that changes the meaning of someone's statement or actions is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special effects and music should be used sparingly and must not alter the truthfulness of the narrative. Any re-creations of past scenes must be clearly marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation Review & Potential Disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: If judges question possible image manipulation, entrants must provide original camera files on request; failure may lead to disqualification and awards may be vacated even after judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges may privately discuss suspected manipulation; committee decisions on eligibility/integrity are final. Requested original files will be asked between specified dates for finalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Commercially Conflicted Work / Branded Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Filmmakers/photographers cannot be paid by anyone with a commercial stake in the story and branded content will not be accepted; work created as sponsored content or for a company/brand/entity is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work done as a team photographer/videographer or on assignment for the organization represented in the story is prohibited in many categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candid Scenes Must Not Be Set Up; Re-creations Must Be Marked
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes presented as candid must not be set up, directed, or controlled; any re-creations to illustrate past events must be clearly labeled as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies across divisions and formats to maintain viewer trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Period & Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries accepted via online portal from December 22, 2025 through 11:59 P.M. PT on January 18, 2026 (and images must be made/published between Jan 1–Dec 31, 2025 unless otherwise noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portal goes live Dec 22, 2025. Questions will be answered up to 12 hours before the final deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Fees, Membership & Fee Waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry is free for NPPA members in good standing at the close of the contest; non-members pay $90. Membership status checked at closing; unpaid non-member entries may be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entering on behalf of others, you cannot use your membership to waive fees for others — each entrant must be a member or pay. On team entries, if one team member is an NPPA member, the entry fee is waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Limits per Entrant / Counting of Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entrant may submit up to 20 total entries across any combination of disciplines; multiple entries in one category count toward this total. A single work may not be entered on its own in more than one division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: two images in one category count as two of the 20 entries. A photo may be entered both as a single image and as part of a story/portfolio; a video may be entered as single and as part of a compilation — each counts separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-Division & Category-Specific Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some divisions and categories have additional restrictions (e.g., entry counts, formats, eligibility); entrants must read individual category descriptions for constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure how to classify an entry, contact the provided contest email for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Still Photojournalism Judging Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges look at technical excellence and composition, but the key factor is the journalism demonstrated — storytelling relevance, community impact, clarity of the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are meant to tell stories that help communities understand trends/issues. This division recognizes individual photojournalists; no team categories for stills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Still Photojournalism Eligibility & Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Work must have been made with intent of journalistic publication; sponsored content or work for brands/companies is not allowed. All visible photo credits or publication names must be removed from captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers may be staff or independent; entrants must ensure pictures provide accurate and fair representations and must not mislead audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited Image Types (still)
rubrics_metrics.description: No multiple exposures, panoramas or stitched photos (in-camera or software) will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such images will be disallowed at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image File Format, Dimensions and Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Images must be JPG, saved as RGB (not CMYK), sized at least 3000 pixels on the long dimension, with quality setting High (9/12 or 8/10) and file size no more than 5 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each image should be saved as an RGB JPG. File size limit and pixel dimensions are enforced for judging and archiving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image Metadata (IPTC) Required Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Required IPTC metadata fields: Caption/Description, City/State/Province/Country, Date (date image was made), Photographer and Credit/Byline (consistent across images), Source, Copyright, Contact Email, Contact Phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions must be written in English and follow basic AP style (see Caption Guide). Use consistent photographer name formatting across images. Metadata can be entered via Photo Mechanic, Bridge, Lightroom, MediaPro, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption Requirements & Structure (Caption Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions must be accurate, answer basic journalism questions, be in English, follow AP style, and use a specific structure for the first sentence: who/what (present tense), city/state/province/country, and date (absolute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First sentence identifies subjects/action and location and date (e.g., 'Monday, December 15, 2025'). Must attribute actions not seen (e.g., 'according to police'). Names listed left-to-right. Second sentence (optional) provides context/significance; when in doubt, omit second sentence. Prefer no more than two concise sentences. For story categories, first image caption block must include an overall story description up to 100 words. Portrait captions must state that the photo is posed/directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Naming & Ordering for Stories/Portfolios
rubrics_metrics.description: Files in story and portfolio categories must begin with sequence numbers (01, 02, etc.) so judges see them in the intended order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence numbering and correct ordering are required to preserve story flow; thumbnails and ordering tools available in the online submission interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove Identifying Credits from Captions (but may remain in metadata)
rubrics_metrics.description: All images MUST have credits removed from the visible caption fields; names or publication credits should not appear in the caption (they may remain in other metadata fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should strip visible credit lines to preserve blind judging and consistency; the judges will rely on other metadata fields where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare to Provide Camera Original Files on Request
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants may be required to submit original camera files for images that proceed to final stages; failure to provide them may result in disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules specify a window when files will be requested (example dates provided in the rules). Keep originals and be ready to provide them quickly if asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove Personal Tags, Ratings, or Color Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must remove any personal tags, ratings or color codes from files prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such embedded data can reveal identities or editorial processes; remove them to comply with contest policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Editing Judging Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will consider design, layout and innovative uses of technology, but weigh most heavily the quality of storytelling — how photos are considered, sequenced and presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries will be judged based on how effectively the photos and storytelling inform and entertain readers. Entrants should document behind-the-scenes/editorial work in a provided narrative field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Editing Submission Format & Presentation Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspaper/magazine entries must be converted to JPG, saved as RGB, at least 3000 pixels tall; double-page spreads should be combined into one JPG so judges can see the full spread; multiple-page entries should be entered as individual JPGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital category entries should submit URLs; paywalled sites must provide login credentials for judges. For online galleries, thumbnails and links must be provided and missing thumbnails may disqualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital/Online Entries & Paywall Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital category entries should be submitted as URLs; for sites behind paywalls provide login/password for judges to access the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation entries without thumbnails or required links may be disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video/Video Editing Division Judging Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will evaluate videos based on technical excellence, storytelling, and demonstrated journalism; the critical factor is the quality of the journalism and audience comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The division recognizes both reporting (filming) and editing craft; judges consider both the reporting process and the editing process as appropriate to category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Roles & Eligibility Definitions (VJ, SVJ, Editor, Reporter/Field Producer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrant role categories are defined: Video Journalist (VJ) — at least 90% filmed by entrant; Solo Video Journalist (SVJ) — films/reports/writes/edits and filmed at least 90% and is sole editor (no nat sound-only SVJ entries); Editor — responsible for editing process; Reporter/Field Producer — collaborates with visual journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These role definitions determine which categories entrants may enter; some categories are combined or specific to the craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Technical Specs & Upload Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos must be mp4 format at 1080p resolution, compressed for smooth online playback, and require a thumbnail upload; thumbnails missing may lead to disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may use familiar compression tools (Handbrake recommended). Thumbnails should be JPG 1920x1080 for video entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Entry Limits & Station/Year Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: General limit: maximum of 4 entries per individual in each story category; Station of the Year entries limited to 1 per station; entrants may submit to each '- of the Year' award they are eligible for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual may be eligible for multiple '- of the Year' categories. Station entries have special compilation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Video / Presentation / Innovation Judging Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are judged primarily on journalism, storytelling and impact; presentation/innovation categories also judge design, interactivity and engagement as part of the whole experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online Video entries are click-to-play stories judged on the video alone. Innovation and Presentation categories require web links and thumbnails; videos longer than 10 minutes should be entered in Documentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual vs Team Entry Definitions & Team Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual entry means a single visual journalist filmed/edited/produced at least 90% of the work; team entries may have unlimited size but should include a note explaining the role of each credited person if not delineated in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple bylines exist, consider entering a team category or include an explanation of division of labor. Team members must be listed in the submission form; team membership affects fee waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary Division Scope & Technical Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary division honors long-form video storytelling for any platform; videos must be mp4 at 1080p and compressed for smooth playback, with thumbnails required and team fields for credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentaries may have been made for broadcast, OTT, streaming or other release; follow same upload & team rules as other video divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thumbnail Requirements for Video & Presentation Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Thumbnails are required for video entries and certain presentation entries; video thumbnails should be 1920x1080 JPGs; missing thumbnails may cause disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thumbnails are uploaded during the submission process (after the main media upload) and are used for judge review and presentation entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English Video Language Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-English language videos may be entered but must be subtitled; judges may not be fluent in other languages and subtitles aid comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate subtitles so judges can fairly evaluate the journalism and storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Interface & Caption Import Behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions are automatically read from metadata on upload (if in correct field) and can be edited on the subsequent pages in the submission interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on server load, it may take time for captions to be encoded/displayed; remove credits or identifying info during this step if needed.
